clue.text: Brilliance reflected by chapter in story

indicators.note: something reflected in a mirror appears back to front, so the built word is read backwards
the chapter's letter sits inside the word for story

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A dazzling quality is mirrored by one chapter of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside TALE to give TACLE, and 'reflected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy success or dazzling effect is the French-derived sense of the word, a synonym of brilliance.

clue.text: Stop sending mobile messages to uninitiated sort of upper class?

indicators.note: without initials, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: sending messages by mobile phone is texting
U stands for upper class, as in 'U and non-U' usage
the suffix -ish means sort of, rather

explanation.surface: A complaint about the upper class texting each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninitiated' cuts the first letter of TEXTING to EXTING. U for upper class comes from a 1950s British essay on 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a fire or end something entirely is to stop it.

clue.text: One of several popes in trouble occasionally

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Popes, the clue suggests, get into trouble now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run across 'trouBLE Occasionally'; 'occasionally' looks like a regular-letters signal but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen popes, and a fourteenth elected in 2025, have taken this name, so it is one of several.

clue.text: Mortar board attachment plastered slates

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Roof slates have been plastered over, with a builder's mortarboard to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A mortarboard is both a plasterer's board and a square academic cap; 'plastered' scrambles SLATES.
explanation.definitionFit: The square academic cap has a hanging bunch of threads fixed to its top.

clue.text: I hope this isn't like wax in water

definitions.text: I hope this isn't like wax in water

parts.words: I hope this isn't like wax in water
parts.note: the setter speaks of the puzzle itself, hoping it cannot be called by the word that describes how wax behaves in water: impossible to dissolve, or impossible to solve

explanation.walkthrough: The word has two senses: of a substance, unable to dissolve; of a problem, unable to be solved. Wax shows the first; the setter fears the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax will not dissolve in water, and a puzzle nobody can crack is the same word in its problem-solving sense.

clue.text: Serious reduction of proximity in the situation

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the one for the situation

parts.note: it can mean the situation, as in 'this is it'

indicators.note: a reduction makes the word shorter by its last letter

parts.note: proximity is nearness

explanation.surface: Someone is grave about cutting the closeness in the present state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction of' docks the last letter, and 'in' places the result inside a short word for 'the situation', as in 'this is it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sincere and not joking is to mean it seriously, so the phrase is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Offended valour catching knight up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top
the word for valour catches the knight's letter inside it

parts.note: guts means courage or valour
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A brave man is hurt when a knight is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts N inside GUTS to make GNUTS, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hurt or upset by a remark is to be stung by it.

clue.text: Old port and pig in fat

indicators.note: the animal goes inside the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: An aged port wine served with pork in dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old port' reads as vintage wine; it is the old word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard was the former sailing term for the left side of a ship, later replaced by port.

clue.text: Nick bids lag to reform recidivism

indicators.note: reforming means remaking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner tells an old lag to go straight, all about reoffending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' (British slang for prison) and 'lag' (a convict) set a jail scene; 'to reform' scrambles the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Relapsing into bad ways after improvement is what a reoffender does.

clue.text: Detect unusual sensitivity over years

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes first

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is an uncanny sensitivity

explanation.surface: Picking up an odd sensitivity that has lasted years.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something is to detect it.

clue.text: One's prepared for wedding and avowedly faithful, therefore

indicators.note: to avow is to declare out loud, so the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: faithful is true and therefore is so, giving 'true so' when said

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready for a wedding swears loyalty, and so sounds devoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avowedly' signals the sound: 'true so' said aloud gives the French-derived word for a bride's outfit and linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen is assembled in advance, so it is something prepared for a wedding.

clue.text: Summary rejection of impatient waiter?

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: someone waiting impatiently walks up and down, a pacer

explanation.surface: A brief report of a restless waiter getting turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns PACER round. The waiter is not a restaurant server but someone waiting, and pacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short restatement of the main points is a summary, the shortened form of recapitulation.

clue.text: German man and US soldier in long periods after catch 22's situation?

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the word for catch in the answer

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them
Herr is the German for Mr, a German man

indicators.note: the soldier's letters go inside the long periods

parts.note: eons are very long periods of time
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A German and an American soldier spend ages caught in a Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: '22's' points to the answer at 22 down, the Devil, whose home is hell, the region below; the question mark flags the cheeky second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is traditionally the region below, so the lower world is where the Devil is placed; the phrase also jokes about the body.

clue.text: You might have loads, rolling in it, after laundering

definitions.text: You might have loads, rolling in it, after laundering

parts.words: You might have loads, rolling in it, after laundering
parts.note: reads like a rich crook who has laundered money; really a machine that tumbles loads of washed clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in it' and 'laundering' suggest money laundering and wealth, but the loads are washing.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine spins wet laundry in a heated drum after it has been washed.

clue.text: Whatever happens, queen's gown must exchange hands!

indicators.note: the left and right hands, L and R, swap places

parts.note: a queen's gown is a regal dress

explanation.surface: A queen orders that her gown be handed over, come what may.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'regal dress' the L (left) and R (right) swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something regardless means doing it whatever happens, despite everything.

clue.text: Muslim community let me see mother

parts.note: um is the hesitating noise of someone thinking, 'let me see'
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone asks to look at their mother while visiting a Muslim community.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic word for the worldwide community of Islamic believers, used in English.

clue.text: China possibly has a problem with corruption

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzling problem
vice is moral corruption

explanation.surface: China, the country, faces a problem with official corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: China is not the country but crockery: a set of cups, saucers and teapot may be china.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of cups, saucers and pot is often made of porcelain, so china is an example.

clue.text: Lumber harbouring sheep tick or fly

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so the tick goes inside

parts.note: to lumber someone with a burden is to saddle them with it
a ked is a sheep tick, a parasite of sheep

explanation.surface: A lumbering sheep carrying ticks or flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like another insect beside the tick; it is the verb, to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off in a hurry is to fly, in the sense of flee.

clue.text: Difficult to trust European when locked in boot

indicators.note: these letters are shut inside the word for boot

parts.note: a welly is a rubber boot, short for wellington
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A shifty European ends up shut in a car boot.
explanation.walkthrough: Boot is a welly, a British rubber boot, not a car boot; EAS goes inside after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sly like the animal is shifty, so not to be trusted.

clue.text: Feels wretched and faces receding pride

indicators.note: wretched suggests something in a bad state, so the letters of feels are knocked into a new order
receding means going backwards, so the word for faces is read in reverse

parts.note: to face someone is to meet them, so faces is meets

explanation.surface: Someone feels miserable and confronts a loss of pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' turns FEELS into SELFE; 'receding' turns MEETS into STEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-respect and a good opinion of oneself is what pride means in its positive sense.

clue.text: Turkish currency note in possession of Inland Revenue

indicators.note: the note holds the tax office's letters, as if owning them

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
IR is the abbreviation of the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A Turkish banknote ends up held by the British tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the British tax office until 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira is the unit of money used in Turkey, and once in Italy.

clue.text: The greatest stout brewing involves malt primarily

indicators.note: involves means includes within, so the picked letter goes inside
brewing stirs things up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
primarily points to the first letter

explanation.surface: The finest stout is brewed with malt above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' makes UTOST of STOUT, which 'involves' M from 'malt primarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost means extreme or greatest, as in the utmost importance.

clue.text: Stopped accepting "pathetic front" label for the underprivileged

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other pieces go inside the word for stopped

parts.note: an engine that has stopped has died
sad means pathetic, pitiable
the van is the front of an army or movement
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A protest stopped after a feeble front group was branded as speaking for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts SADVANTAG inside DIED. 'front' here is van, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Those without the advantages of others are described as deprived or underprivileged.

clue.text: Terror experienced on rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to have experienced something is to have lived through it

explanation.surface: Fear felt when getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: A terror is a naughty child, a little devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little terror or a little devil.

clue.text: Fur's minute stain

parts.note: ink can stain, and an ink blot is a stain

explanation.surface: A fur coat has a tiny mark on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute reads as tiny, but it is the unit of time, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mink is the animal and the luxurious fur taken from it.

clue.text: Polled neat will furnish pastoral scene

indicators.note: a polled animal has had its horns, or head, removed, so the first letter goes

parts.note: neat means tidy
'll is the short form of will, as in I'll

explanation.surface: Hornless cattle make a picture of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polled' and 'neat' suggest hornless cattle; in fact polled beheads TIDY to IDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A charming picture of simple rural life, the kind of happy country scene a pastoral poem describes.

clue.text: Movie aged badly in its interactive spin-off?

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A film that has dated poorly lives on in a game based on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles MOVIE AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played on screen is interactive, and many are made as tie-ins to films.

clue.text: Ability to hit top marks?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or top, with the 1 read as the letter I
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Skill at hitting the target earns top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of A1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Good aim is a marksman's skill in hitting the target.

clue.text: Perhaps setter's alternative is to conceal clue with spoonerism

indicators.note: a Spoonerism swaps the opening sounds of two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: to bury something is to conceal it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's other option is to hide the clue with a slip of the tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter here is the dog, not the compiler. Swapping the first sounds of 'bury clue' (said 'berry') gives the name of an Irish terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kerry blue is an Irish terrier, another breed of dog one might keep instead of a setter.

clue.text: Race results multiply daily

definitions.meaning: the results of a race are the recorded durations of the runners
to multiply is to do the sum written with the x sign
a daily is a newspaper, here the one printing this very puzzle

explanation.definitionFit: Race results are the clocked durations, multiply is the arithmetic word, and the daily is the London newspaper itself.
